record.what_it_does: Pay-as-you-go APIs for SEO data: SERP, keywords, backlinks, on-page, and business data.
record.auth_notes: The REST API accepts only HTTP Basic auth, using the API login and password from the API Access tab in the dashboard. The REST API has no OAuth, so a multi-user toolkit would have each user enter their own login and password. The vendor-hosted MCP server is different: it defaults to OAuth 2.0 with Bearer tokens and accepts login and password env vars as a fallback. That OAuth applies only to the MCP server, not to api.dataforseo.com.
record.access_notes: Anyone who registers gets API credentials. The Sandbox (sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3/) is free for every registered user and returns sample data. New accounts get a $1 trial credit. Beyond that, live data needs a prepaid balance, and the minimum top-up is $50. There is no subscription or recurring fee, and funds don't expire.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers SERP, Keywords Data, DataForSEO Labs, Backlinks, On-Page, Domain Analytics, Content Analysis, Business Data, App Data, Merchant and AI Optimization. Each has many task_post, task_get and live endpoints, well over 50 in total. The official OpenAPI 3.x YAML (dataforseo/OpenApiDocumentation) describes every endpoint.
record.mcp_notes: The remote endpoint is https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp, which the vendor calls its "official DataForSEO remote endpoint". It uses OAuth 2.0 by default. Repo: github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript. The npm package dataforseo-mcp-server runs locally. The vendor page also describes an "official DataForSEO MCP image" for Docker.
record.blocker_notes: Users need their own DataForSEO account. Live data needs a funded balance (minimum top-up $50, after a $1 trial credit). Because the REST API uses Basic auth, each user enters credentials instead of going through an OAuth flow. Development and testing can run free against the Sandbox.
